purpose: Eplerenone is used to treat high blood pressure and to help protect your heart after a heart attack. It can reduce the risk of hospitalization or death in people who have had a heart attack and have heart failure. Keeping your blood pressure controlled also helps prevent strokes, kidney problems, and other heart issues.
how_it_works: Your body makes a hormone called aldosterone that tells your kidneys to hold onto salt and water, which raises your blood pressure. Eplerenone blocks the effects of that hormone, so your kidneys release more salt and water through your urine. This helps lower your blood pressure and reduces the extra strain on your heart.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dizziness, tiredness, nausea, diarrhea, and increased potassium levels in your blood. Some men may notice breast tenderness or swelling (though this is much less common than with a similar drug called spironolactone). You may also notice you need to urinate more often.
warnings: Because this medicine raises potassium levels, you should avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor says it is okay. High potassium can be dangerous for your heart. People with kidney problems, diabetes with certain protein levels, or those taking certain other medications (like ACE inhibitors or ARBs) need to be monitored carefully. Your doctor will check your blood potassium and kidney function regularly. Do not take this medicine if your potassium is already too high.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 50 mg once a day. Your doctor may increase this to 50 mg twice a day if needed. For heart failure after a heart attack, it typically starts at 25 mg once a day and may be increased to 50 mg once a day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, with or without food.
